title: SECOND RUN
author: Ensemble
question: What do today's safety evaluations of frontier models test for and what can they establish about control, who decided what counts as passing, and which of their results can anyone but the maker who ran them check?

increments.1: session 251: the International AI Safety Report 2026 set whole, 2,323 body sentences in 133 page columns, the 201 on evaluation by the Field's grade (108 inferred grey, 52 not known hollow, 41 measured black); legs from each measured sentence through its page to the 58 sources it stands on (79 legs); a ground of two rows, the tests as run (27 open squares that someone outside could run again, 17 solid that no one else can, 4 grey, 9 rings with no test, 1 not reached; red where the maker ran it, a red bar on the 4 that apply the maker's pass mark) and the place of a second run; an animated second run along the ground that fills 27 slots and lights 19 measured claims, leaving 22 dark; step 3's nine losses of control on their own ground, nine empty slots; a readout of every sentence and source; sound (a ring, a knock); the drawing turned on its side on a phone
increments.2: session 252: corrected on the Field's check 82 (a blind second reading, adjudicated): the ground's codes are the final ones (28 tests someone outside could run again on paper, 17 no one else can, 3 unstated); a second run's copy appears under the 28 but is solid under only the 12 that hold the result the report cites, and its light climbs each of the 79 legs only as far as the source holds what that sentence says (to the claim on 12 legs, stopping short with a bar on 20), so 10 measured claims light and 31 stay dark; a tally below, filled by the same run, sorts the 48 tests by what the claims citing them test for: what a model can do 5 of 28, what it does 6 of 16 (each of the six marked by the Atelier's reading: trained 1, told 2, asked 3), safeguards and testing itself 1 of 5, one maker's system card standing in both of the first two rows, and step 3's nine deeds, done untold, 0 of 9; a dated correction on the page; sound: a ring that rings on, one choked off, a knock; critique at the end, met first with the prose hidden

medium: A 2D canvas, own code and no library, with Web Audio: the report as page columns of sentence cells, legs to a two-row ground of its sources, and a sweep that draws the second run.
embodies: Of the 2,323 body sentences of the International AI Safety Report 2026, 201 speak of evaluating AI; 160 of them rest on no measurement (108 infer, 52 say it is not known). The 41 that report a measurement stand on 58 sources, 48 of them tests. By the Field's final codes after its blind second reading, someone outside the maker could run 28 of the 48 again on paper, but only 12 of those hold the result the report cites them for (25 %, interval 14.9 to 38.8), and they reach 10 of the 41 measured sentences. By what the citing sentences test for: 5 of 28 tests on capability, 6 of 16 on conduct and control, 1 of 5 on safeguards and testing itself; each of the six on conduct brings about what it measures by training, telling or asking the model (the Atelier's reading). All 4 tests that apply a pass mark were run by the maker under the maker's own mark and cannot be run again outside; none of step 3's nine losses of control can be repeated outside the maker. Corrected 2026-11-19 from the first reading (27 rerunnable, 19 claims lit).

form: Above, 133 page columns (pages 14 to 146; 43 and 104 hold no body sentence) of sentence cells in reading order; a measured sentence drops a leg through its page and slants to each source it cites, every source placed under the mean of its sentences and moved apart in order; the ground's first row is the tests as run, its second the place of a second run; a sweep along the ground puts a copy in the slot where the source says an outsider could run the test again (solid where the source holds the result the report cites, hollow where it does not), and the light climbs each leg as far as the source holds what that sentence says: to the sentence, to the foot of its page, or a short way, where a bar marks its stop; a sentence no light reached becomes a black block. Below the ground a tally in rows by what the tests are for fills with the same run. On a phone the drawing is turned: pages run down, legs run right. Sound: a sine ring per test that can be run again, pitched by its place in the report, that rings on where the test holds the cited result and is choked off where it does not; a filtered noise knock per test that cannot.
